text.p: Following are the main stories in Croatian newspapers on Thursday. Reuters has not verified them and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Tourists heading for the Adriatic coast between mid June and September will be given discounts on bus, train and plane fares.

- The National Defence and Security Council was pleased by U.S. State Secretary Madeleine Albright's recent visit that confirmed the two countries had common interests, it said after a meeting on Wednesday.
- The United Nations transitional authority in Eastern Slavonia said 45,000 dispalced Croatians expressed a desire to return there once the enclave reverts to Zagreb rule in July.
- Retail prices increased by 0.4 percent last month and cost of living by 1.1 percent, while kuna exchange rates remain stable, said national bank's governor Marko Skreb.
- Conditions are met for departure of the U.N. transitional authority in Eastern Slavonia, President Franjo Tudjman said in a meeting with U.N. commissioner for peacekeeping operations Bernard Miyet.
- Croatia signs a contract to recieve $160 million loan from the World Bank for structural adjustment of the financial sector and companies (EFSAL).
- Croatian post office is to introduce the possibility of recieving calls from all telephone booths in Zagreb and 60 percent of those elsewhere in the country.
- The government's comission for demining said there were no mines along the Adriatic, answering warnings by some neighbouring countries that it was not safe for tourists.
- State television is the ruling party's servant, says presidential candidate Zdravko Tomac in a press conference.
- Banks and companies who receive loans from foreign banks will have to register them with the central bank.
- Police discovered a family of three who printed fake money in their loft in the port of Rijeka. -- Zagreb Newsroom, 385 1 4557075
